summary: Build a lookup with a shared initial value.
documentation: fromkeys constructs a dictionary with keys from an iterable and the same initial value for each. Repeated keys collapse into one entry. Dictionary iteration retains the insertion order of distinct keys.
inputs: An iterable of keys and optional initial value.
caution: A mutable default is shared by every key. Use an immutable initial value or create separate mutable values with a comprehension.
scenarios: Initialize attendance flags for an event roster.
Build a lookup of feature names awaiting review.
Create a starting inventory-count map for imported SKU names.
title: Initialize a checklist
problem: Input is a list of task-name strings, possibly repeated. Return an object containing each distinct task name mapped to False. An empty input yields an empty object.
goal: Use dict.fromkeys() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use fromkeys with the immutable Boolean False.
